Divine heredity may disclose to creatures attributes that are not disclosed in the Creators (17:3.3).
017:46: The Reflective Spirits are transmitters and conservers. Unlike the official records kept by the angelic recorders, true spiritual values are gathered by reflectivity and preserved in the living minds of the family of the Infinite Spirit (17:3.5-3.6). Reflectivity is also the mechanism for gathering news and broadcasting decrees, and, contrary to appearances, it is not automatic but highly personal and intelligent (17:3.7-3.8).

018:1: How do the never-failing personalities of the Trinity govern and help the universe, from Paradise down to our constellation?
018:4: In Paper 17 we saw the seven Supreme Spirit groups, the functional family of the Infinite Spirit. Now Paper 18 introduces the administrators born directly of the Paradise Trinity—the seven orders of Supreme Trinity Personalities. All of them were designed by the Trinity for specific service (18:0.1).
018:5: Their number is fixed and final; no more are being created (18:0.9). They represent the administrative policies and the justice of the Trinity, and they form a complete line of administration reaching from the Father’s Paradise spheres to the capitals of the local universe constellations (18:0.10). Because they share the essence of divinity, there is never any danger of failure or possibility of rebellion among them (18:0.11).
018:6: Where, then, does each of these seven orders work and what does it do, and whom will we meet as we ascend along the way?
018:8: ⟦Q 18:1.5⟧The Paradise Creators respect the privacy and sanctity of personality even in their lowly creatures.⟦/Q⟧ (18:1.5)
018:17: The seven secret spheres of the Father
018:38: Each of the seven worlds of the innermost Paradise circuit is jointly governed by ten Trinitized Secrets of Supremacy. Seven of them each head one of seven divisions, and the remaining three represent the Father, the Son, and the Spirit respectively (18:1.1-1.2). The directors of each sphere resemble the Deity or Deity union that the sphere reveals (18:1.3).
018:39: Their work has to do with the intimate and personal contact of the Deities with the seven basic groups of beings, so it is truly a secret of Supremacy. To one who has attained divine perfection the Deities are like an open book, yet no one can know all the personal relations of Deity with each creature (18:1.4-1.5). These secret worlds always remain a test of loyalty even for high beings (18:1.6).
018:41: Each of the billion worlds of Havona is governed by one Eternal of Days. They have ruled from eternity without changing places, appearing to all the will creatures of their realms and presiding over the planetary conclaves (18:2.1-2.2). When they are absent, a Trinity Teacher Son directs in their place (18:2.2).
018:42: Each of them has developed his sphere according to his own ideas and ideals, and though they visit one another, they never imitate. That is why every world of Havona is wholly unlike every other (18:2.3-2.4). We speak of going “upward” to Paradise, but it would be more correct to say we go “inward” (18:2.4).
018:44: The Ancients of Days were all trinitized at the same time, and the trinitization of these twenty-one is recorded on the first line of the personality records of the universe of universes. Hence their name, “⟦Q 18:3.4⟧Ancients of Days⟦/Q⟧” (18:3.4). They always rule three together (18:3.5).
018:57: Uniform administration and harmony over the diversity
018:59: They are the most powerful of the direct rulers of the time-space creations, and they alone pass final sentence on the eternal extinction of will creatures (18:3.7). Yet because this rule was not earned through experience, they will one day yield their place to the Supreme Being, the experiential sovereign, and become his vicegerent rulers (18:3.8-3.9).
018:61: ⟦Q 18:3.9⟧The Supreme Being is achieving the sovereignty of the seven superuniverses by experiential service just as a Creator Son experientially earns the sovereignty of his local universe.⟦/Q⟧ (18:3.9)

Most of the administrators under them are seasoned beings who served apprenticeships with the Eternals of Days in Havona (18:4.6).
018:65: After passing through the minor sector, we will meet the Perfections of Days when we go to the headquarters of the major sector, Splandon. They personally administer the pledges of the graduates of the major sector schools, and before reaching Uversa we will meet all thirty Perfections of Days of Orvonton (18:4.7, 4.9).

018:71: The seventy worlds of the major sector

In nature they are co-ordinate with the Perfections of Days, but in administrative authority they are subordinate (18:5.1). The minor sector governments deal chiefly with the great physical problems of the superuniverse, and the minor sector spheres are the headquarters of the Master Physical Controllers (18:5.3).
018:78: So it is seldom that all three are together at the capital, but at least one is always on duty (18:5.4). Every one of us will someday come to know the three Recents of Days of the minor sector of Ensa (18:5.5).
018:80: The “of Days” orders do not administer below the superuniverse governments; in the local universes they serve only as counselors. One Union of Days is stationed in each local universe as the representative of the Trinity and of the Father (18:6.1). 018:86: The Perfections of Days of the major sector

018:91: They are not organically connected with the local universe government and act only at the request of the local authorities (18:6.5). 018:93: The Faithfuls of Days are the Paradise advisers who counsel the Vorondadek rulers of the hundred constellations of each local universe. They received their name because they are so supremely devoted and faithful to the welfare of the constellations to which they are assigned (18:7.1-7.2). They take no part in administration unless invited, and their residences are truly modest compared with the homes of the Vorondadek rulers (18:7.2, 7.4).
018:94: The regime of Trinity origin ends with them in the constellations. The administration of the local systems and the inhabited worlds is entirely in the hands of beings born in the local universe (18:7.5).
018:96: Paper 18 shows us the ladder of Trinity personalities that reaches from Paradise down to the constellations. At the very center they guard the personal secrets between Deity and creature; in Havona each develops an original world of his own; in the superuniverses they set uniform justice over the diverse creations; and in the local universes and constellations they do not rule but counsel and stand by. They are perfect beings who never fail, but because their authority was not earned through experience, they will one day yield their place to the Supreme Being, the experiential sovereign. We will meet them one after another on the path of ascension, and in all these meetings we will learn that the Creators respect the personality even of the lowliest creature.

019:1: How do the wisdom, counsel, and judgment of the Trinity become living personalities who serve the universe?
019:4: In Paper 18 we saw the seven orders of Supreme Trinity Personalities who govern from Paradise down to the constellations. Now Paper 19 deals with other beings who come from the same Trinity—the co-ordinate Trinity-origin beings. The author of this paper is himself one of them, a Divine Counselor (19:0.1).
019:5: They include the Trinity Teacher Sons, the three groups of superuniverse administrators, the mysterious Inspired Trinity Spirits, and the Havona natives and Paradise Citizens. Except for the Teacher Sons and the Inspired Spirits, their numbers are all fixed (19:0.2-0.9).
019:6: What, then, are these beings, and how do the wisdom, counsel, and judgment of the Trinity become living personalities that reach even us who are evolving?
019:8: In this juridical trio the Perfector of Wisdom would be the “I was,” the Divine Counselor the “I will be,” but the Universal Censor is always “I am.” (19:4.4)
019:30: The Trinity Teacher Sons are beings of dual status: Trinity in origin, yet devoted in function to the service of divine sonship. They are liaison beings who bridge the gap between Trinity-origin personalities and dual-origin personalities, and they are the supreme co-ordinating personalities of Trinity origin (19:1.1, 1.4).
019:31: In this connection the author explains why this revelation begins not with man but with Paradise. The method of going only from the lower to the higher can show origins, but it can hardly show destiny. A true perspective is gained only by studying origin, history, and destiny together (19:1.5-1.6, 1.12).
019:33: Errors of looking only from the bottom up
019:36: Utterly failing to perceive the final evolutionary goal
019:40: How a being became what it is does not show its true present character

019:48: The Perfectors of Wisdom personalize the wisdom of divinity in the superuniverses. There are exactly seven billion of them, one billion in each superuniverse. They do not reflect the wisdom of the Trinity; they are that wisdom itself (19:2.1, 2.3).
019:49: Wisdom has two origins: the wisdom that comes from the divine insight of perfect beings, and the wisdom that evolutionary creatures gain through experience. Neither alone can fathom the full potential of wisdom, so the Perfectors of Wisdom always work together with administrators of ascending mortal origin (19:2.4-2.5).
019:55: The personal experience of evolutionary creatures
019:56: Mighty Messengers · Those without Name and Number · Those High in Authority
019:59: The Divine Counselors are the counsel of Deity itself to the seven superuniverses; twenty-one billion of them serve, three billion in each superuniverse (19:3.1). When one Perfector of Wisdom, seven Divine Counselors, and one Universal Censor come together, they form a tribunal of Trinity divinity, the highest mobile advisory body in the universes of time and space. The verdicts of this tribunal have never once been reversed by the Ancients of Days (19:3.4).
019:60: When divine counsel is joined with the experiential counsel of associates perfected by evolution, its conclusions become not only perfect but replete. Only the Paradise bestowal Sons, who are both God and man, come nearer than this to the united attitude of creature and Creator (19:3.6-3.7).
019:62: There are exactly eight billion Universal Censors, and they are the very judgment of the Trinity. Even the Ancients of Days do not pass judgment without a Censor (19:4.1). When all the testimony, wisdom, and counsel have been gathered, the Censor gives the true and unerring summation of it all, and when he speaks there is no appeal (19:4.5).
019:77: The author says that the Censors seem to combine facts and findings so as to create new meanings and values, and that their verdicts are unpredictable, as if they were in liaison with the Deity Absolute (19:4.6-4.7). The Perfectors of Wisdom, Divine Counselors, and Universal Censors, together with the seven Supreme Trinity Personalities, make up the ten groups of Stationary Sons of the Trinity, a little more than thirty-seven billion in number (19:4.8).
019:79: The Inspired Trinity Spirits are one of the few wholly secret orders. They are probably superpersonal spirits, and even Trinity-origin beings can recognize them only under certain conditions. Only the Solitary Messengers sense their presence, like a magnetic needle (19:5.1-5.5). Even as the author writes this, such a Spirit is within twenty-five feet of him (19:5.7).
019:80: The Solitary Messengers feel a similar qualitative disturbance on planets indwelt by Thought Adjusters. This suggests that the Adjusters and the Inspired Spirits are related in some way (19:5.6). If the Teacher Sons are devoted to conscious enlightenment, the Inspired Spirits may be teachers who work by superconscious techniques, for there are spiritual truths whose reception is actually hindered by self-consciousness (19:5.9).

Ascending mortals and Havona natives are of great benefit to each other. Through friendship with them we are compensated for our early spiritual poverty, and through contact with us they go beyond the limits of an experience that has only ever been perfect (19:6.2).
019:86: Unlike the Stationary Sons, the Havona natives can evolve in status, and some of them enter the Corps of the Finality. Since no more are being created, their number is decreasing, and it is conjectured that new residents will be mixed into the Havona of the future (19:6.3-6.4).

019:101: More than three thousand orders of Paradise Citizens live on Paradise. They are not directly concerned with the ascension plan, so they have not been revealed to us in detail, and together with the Havona natives they are called the Paradise-Havona personalities (19:7.1-7.2). None of those whom the Trinity brought into being has ever gone astray, yet in the highest sense all of them have free will (19:7.3). They travel freely without seraphim, and the author tells us that it took him 109 days to come from Uversa to Urantia (19:7.4).

The Havona natives too go beyond the limits of their experience through friendship with us. In this universe where perfection and experience fill each other out, the author urges us to look at man from Paradise downward. A true perspective opens when we see not only origin but destiny, and as we travel that road we will long use faith and depend on revelation.

020:1: Why do the Sons of Paradise go to the trouble of coming down to the evolutionary worlds in the likeness of mortals like us?
020:4: In Paper 19 we met beings who originate in the Paradise Trinity, the Stationary Sons who govern the superuniverses. Now Paper 20 turns our attention to the very name “Son.” The Sons of God functioning in Orvonton fall into three categories (20:0.1-0.4).
020:5: The descending Sons are personalities directly and divinely created. Ascending sons, such as mortals, gain their status by experiential participation in evolution, and the trinitized sons are a group of composite origin embraced by the Trinity (20:0.5). This paper describes in detail the Sons who come down from Paradise, especially the Magisterial Sons and the Trinity Teacher Sons.
020:6: What, then, do these high Sons do, and why do they choose the path of being born of woman, living, and dying as we do?
020:8: ⟦Q 20:1.11⟧From the standpoint of service, worship, and supplication the Paradise Sons are as one; their spirit is one, and their work is identical in quality and completeness.⟦/Q⟧ (20:1.11)
020:18: Gain their status by experiential participation in evolution
020:20: A group of composite origin embraced by the Trinity
020:22: The descending Sons all have a high and divine origin, and they are devoted to the service of helping lowly creatures of evolutionary origin climb toward Paradise. Seven orders of them are presented; the first three are Paradise Sons and the other four are local universe Sons of God (20:1.1-1.9).
020:27: Michaels — the Universal Father and the Eternal Son
020:29: Avonals — the Eternal Son and the Infinite Spirit
020:31: Daynals — the Father, the Son, and the Spirit
020:33: The Creator Son, the Creative Spirit, and the Father Melchizedek
020:35: The Creator Son and the Creative Spirit — Most Highs, Constellation Fathers
020:37: The Creator Son and the Creative Spirit — System Sovereigns, Planetary Princes
020:39: The Creator Son, the Creative Spirit, and the Ancients of Days
020:41: The Paradise Sons have revealed themselves as creators, ministers, bestowers, judges, teachers, and revealers of truth. In the local universes the Magisterial and Teacher Sons are under the direction of the Creator Son of that realm (20:1.12). The Creator Son has a spiritual drawing power that duplicates in his local universe the spirit gravity of the Eternal Son, and he is personally conscious of the acts and feelings of every descending Son serving in his domain (20:1.13). The Michael order is left to a later paper; this paper deals with the Magisterial and Teacher Sons (20:1.15).
020:43: Each time the absolute concept of the Eternal Son is united with the ideal of loving service conceived by the Infinite Spirit, a new Magisterial Son, an Avonal, comes into being. They are not creators in the personal sense, but they are planetary ministers and judges closely associated with the Michaels in all their work (20:2.1). There are about one billion of them in the grand universe; they are directed by the supreme council of Paradise, and when assigned to a local universe they serve under the direction of its Creator Son (20:2.2).
020:48: Judge at the end of a dispensation and release the sleeping survivors — dozens or hundreds of times
020:50: Incarnated as adults before the bestowal Son — possibly many times
020:52: Born of woman — only once on any planet
020:54: Usually, after an Avonal has passed through seven magisterial and bestowal experiences, he gives other Sons their opportunity and moves on to the personal council of the Creator Son (20:2.8). On the inhabited worlds they are helped by Melchizedeks and archangels, and on bestowal missions they are accompanied by the Brilliant Evening Stars. All the power and authority of the Creator Son stand behind them, so their work is just as effective as if the Creator Son had done it himself (20:2.9).
020:56: The Avonals are the judges of the successive dispensations of the worlds of time. They preside over the awakening of the sleeping survivors, bring to an end an age of suspended justice, and reassign the creatures of space to the tasks of a new age (20:3.1). They may pass sentence on the extinction of a creature’s identity, but only the superuniverse authorities carry it out (20:3.2).
020:61: Without incarnation, coming as unseen spirit beings
020:63: Sometimes incarnated — in the form of an adult
020:67: Whatever the mission, an incarnated Son judges the passing planetary age. When a Paradise Son becomes like one of the people of an evolutionary world, his very presence ends a dispensation and judges the realm (20:3.4).
020:69: On his first magisterial visit an Avonal always incarnates as a fully grown male of the mortal race and appears as a being whom the people of that age can see and touch. All the while his connection with the spiritual forces is not broken (20:4.1-4.2). An incarnated Paradise Son is indwelt by an experienced Adjuster; these Adjusters do not attain personality through fusion, but they are often personalized by the mandate of the Father and form the directing council of Divinington (20:4.3).
020:70: Urantia has never been visited by an Avonal on a magisterial mission. Normally one would have come between the Adamic age and Michael’s bestowal, but the Creator Son’s final bestowal completely upset that order (20:4.4). And since there is Michael’s promise to return, only time will reveal the order of future visits (20:4.5).

021:4: Paper 20 looked at the Magisterial and Teacher Sons among the Paradise Sons and left the Michael order for later. Paper 21 is the story of those Creator Sons. 021:6: Why, then, must these Sons, who already have all creative power, humble themselves and live seven times in the likeness of their own creatures?
021:8: The Creator Sons are achieving the personal realization of the Paradise-divinity potentials bound up in their unfathomable natures. (21:6.4)

Each is the absolute of the Deity concepts that make up his origin (21:1.2).
021:13: A Creator Son’s nature comes equally from both parents, but in actual work some Sons are more like the Father and some more like the Son. 021:15: The Creator Son is the designer, builder, and administrator of the local universe, the basic creative unit of the seven evolutionary superuniverses. From then on he rules not as the Father’s vicegerent but in his own name, as “⟦Q 21:4.5⟧King of Kings and Lord of Lords⟦/Q⟧” (21:4.5). A Creator Son who has completed his bestowals becomes a Master Son, one who has added the experience of a creature to his own nature (21:4.6).
021:59: ⟦Q 21:4.6⟧Why should man bemoan his lowly origin and enforced evolutionary career when the very Gods must pass through an equivalent experience before they are accounted experientially worthy and competent finally and fully to rule over their universe domains!⟦/Q⟧ (21:4.6)

021:69: Embodies the sevenfold attitude of time-space creatures
021:71: Joins Paradise attitude and creature viewpoint into one

022:1: What does it mean for an evolving mortal to receive the embrace of the Trinity and become a Son who helps govern a superuniverse?
022:4: In Papers 20 and 21 we met the descending Sons who come down from Paradise. Paper 22 deals with the third group called Sons of God, the Trinitized Sons of God (22:0.1). What they have in common is that either their origin involved trinitization or they later had the experience of being embraced by the Trinity (22:0.5).
022:5: The trinitized sons are divided into Deity-trinitized Sons, Trinity-embraced Sons, and creature-trinitized Sons. The Deity-trinitized Sons are not revealed, so this paper pictures the other two groups, especially the Trinity-embraced Sons (22:0.2-0.5). The author himself is a Mighty Messenger who was once a mortal.
022:6: By what path, then, do mortals like us receive the embrace of the Trinity, and what do the Sons who have received it do in the superuniverses?
022:8: There is simply nothing in all universal existence which can take the place of actual personal experience. (22:9.7)
022:12: The Trinity-embraced Sons are originally of dual or single origin, but once embraced they are devoted forever to the service of the Trinity. They consist of seven orders of personalities, which are again divided into three classes according to origin and nature (22:1.1-1.9).
022:18: Mighty Messengers, Those High in Authority, Those without Name and Number
022:19: Adjuster-fused mortals who have reached the Corps of the Finality
022:22: Ascendant seraphim, midway creatures, Spirit-fused and Son-fused mortals
022:25: Creature-trinitized sons who have been twice trinitized
022:27: When the Sons of Attainment are embraced, their names are removed from the finaliter rolls, and after a short training in Havona they are assigned to the service of the Ancients of Days (22:1.10). Their associates of Trinity origin are fixed in number, but the embraced Sons are constantly increasing, and not a single one has ever been lost. The Sons of Perfection, however, have sometimes erred in judgment (22:1.13).
022:29: The Mighty Messengers are perfected mortals who have been tested in rebellion or have otherwise proved their loyalty in an equivalent way. They are embraced in classes of seven hundred thousand, and nearly one trillion have been commissioned on Uversa alone (22:2.5).
022:30: The author tells us that he is a Mighty Messenger, that his companion of mortal days also triumphed in the great test and was embraced in the same group, and that the two of them are now dispatched together from Uversa (22:2.6). They act as defenders of individuals and planets before the superuniverse courts, and they are stationed on many worlds as official observers for the Ancients of Days (22:2.8). Because they remember their whole ascending career, they will be able to communicate with us understandingly as soon as we are delivered from the flesh (22:2.9).

022:33: In the superuniverse tribunals they act as prosecutors who present the case for justice. 022:35: Those without Name and Number are ascendant souls who have developed a capacity to worship beyond that of the evolutionary races. 022:52: You mortals who read this message may yourselves ascend to Paradise and attain the Trinity embrace. (22:4.7)

022:59: The Ambassadors are envoys of the Ancients of Days, sent anywhere within the superuniverse, and they are the emergency or reserve corps of the supergovernment. The thousands of tasks they perform have no parallel on Urantia and so cannot be described (22:6.3).
